parts.quote: "Current rating: 3 A AC/DC（AWG #22）", "2.5 mm pitch"; part "B2B-XH-A". Pin 1 +28 V, pin 2 GND (our assignment)

"Maximum repetitive peak reverse voltage VRRM ... 60 V" (SS36); "Maximum average forward rectified current at TL (fig. 1) IF(AV) 3.0 A"; VF "0.75" V at "3.0 A" (SS35, SS36); "Case: SMC (DO-214AB)"; "Polarity: color band denotes the cathode end"; uses include "polarity protection". In series with the input: a reversed supply is blocked (TPS1H100-Q1 p28 "Method 1: Block diode connected with VS. Both the device and load are protected")

unidirectional ("For bidirectional devices use CA suffix (e.g. SMBJ10CA)"; drawn with the Zener symbol, cathode to +28 V); "SMB (DO-214AA)", "600 W ... 10/1000 μs"; Table 1 "SMBJ28A ... 31.1 34.4 ... 28 ... 13.2 45.4": standoff 28 V, clamping 45.4 V at 13.2 A, under the TPS1H100-Q1's 48 V ("withstand 48-V load dump voltage for 400 ms", tps p4); the SMBJ33A's 53.3 V is not

+28V.note: after the diode and the clamp

layout.rules: the diode and TVS at the connector, wide traces (POWER class)

open_questions: SMBJ28A's 28 V standoff equals the nominal bus: above it the TVS starts to leak; the bus's maximum voltage is not set yet (the SMBJ30A's 48.4 V clamp would just exceed the arm switch's 48 V).

SS36: 3.0 A (at its lead temperature) covers about 8 heaters (0.21 A each) and 8 coils (0.15 A) at once; all 16 heater elements and 16 coils together (about 5.8 A) would exceed it: firmware limits what runs together, or a larger diode / an ideal-diode controller.
JST XH's voltage rating not read (the catalogue blocks downloads now); XH 3 A per pin covers the current.
